strongest_rival_threat.rival: Attest (josepha-mayo/attest, Ring-track entrant, MIT, CI, also entering AWS Builder and Open Source)
strongest_rival_threat.why: Attest serves the same people (in-home aides and households) on the same track with the same Ring mechanism. It polls Event History, keeps on_demand records as their own evidence kind, opens WHEP live views and writes each session (opened, closed, state) into signed coverage. Its README says 'Worker-facing pages show the same timeline the coordinator sees before they sign', so the worker already sees brokered live views after the visit. It has been built since 15 Sep and has KMS, signed packs, an offline verifier, an emulator and a signed live-API sweep. A Ring judge who sees both may read OnAir as an Attest feature turned around to face the worker. What Attest does not do, per its README: push notice to the worker during the shift, a two-party agreement on purposes, windows and a private hour, rule classification of each session, or configuration-drift notices. Whether Attest's worker view includes live views opened in the Ring app (as opposed to ones it brokered) is not stated (inference: probably not surfaced as notice).

RNG-3.eligibility_attack:
No hard blocker.

What passes:
- The Rules (section 4, Ring) accept 'Any Ring API, SDK, simulator, or device listed in Ring's developer documentation'. The video must show the project 'working through a simulator or an actual Ring device'. The Playground is in Ring's release notes, and the FAQ names it as a simulator.
- The runtime hook is met by server-side calls to api.amazonvision.com.
- Organizer forum 45309 confirms the Playground is 'the only documented route that needs neither a US device nor an account link'.

Caveats:
1. ring-sandbox is not 'listed in Ring's developer documentation'. It can only support labelled side beats, such as the drift fixture, never the core loop.
2. The concept cites 'Content Policy §12.2'. The clause is §1.2.2. It also says 'Apps must provide to Ring customers easy access to monitoring activity or access logs'. That duty is owed to the Ring customer (the household), about the app's own access. OnAir therefore also needs a household-facing log of its own API calls. Its claim to 'match Ring's direction' is an inference, not policy text.
3. §4.1.1 makes employers responsible for notice and consents. OnAir must not imply it discharges that duty. Keep the 'not legal advice' notice, and make no compliance claims about Connecticut, Washington or any other state.
4. Sharing the account holder's live-view activity with a third party (the worker) needs the account holder's explicit, affirmative consent. The two-party signing covers this; show it on screen.
5. Video rules: credit the CC BY Playground footage on screen if any frame appears. Show no third-party brands or logos, such as nanny agencies or other camera vendors.
6. Not a latent-LLM idea: there is no model in the decision path, and it is not an existing Ring feature (see differentiation).
RNG-3.feasibility_attack:
The 70 h solo estimate is plausible (estimate). The risks sit in the platform, not in the hours.

1. WHEP on the Playground is contested.
   - doorstep-ring got a frame on 23 Sep, but 'Only an offer built by headless Chrome works'.
   - Attest's signed sweep on 30 Sep lists WHEP as a fail: 'needs streaming hardware on the account'.
   - The field-of-view frame and the 'Check the front door' beat both depend on WHEP. Use a browser WebRTC offer (the ring-api-helloworld Next.js path), never a server-side client.

2. In production, TAKE removes video for partners. FAQ Q10 says a TAKE device stays callable, but 'video requests return encrypted content, so your app cannot read recordings or snapshots, or open a live stream'. TAKE is rolling out as the default from September 2026, so the brokered viewer and the field-of-view frame would fail for most real users. The metadata core (history, configurations, status) should keep working (inference from 'visible and callable'). E2EE devices drop out of the API entirely.

3. The self-audit contradicts itself.
   - is_third_party_reviewed is defined as 'whether your partner app has previously downloaded media (video or image) for this event'.
   - OnAir opens WHEP sessions itself, so the panel's promise ('OnAir never pulled media') is false by construction.
   - Whether WHEP flips the flag is unknown. Attest also reports that its own snapshot media requests create on_demand records.

4. Attribution can only be by time-matching. The organizer (45309) confirms history attributes are exactly event_type, is_third_party_reviewed, start and end, so nothing says who opened a session. A Ring-app session that overlaps OnAir's own session will be misattributed.

5. The event_types filter is ignored. Attest reports this, and the forum poster saw singular forms ignored. Filter client-side.

6. Latency is unmeasured. Records carry start and end, so they may appear only after a session ends. Partner sessions cap at 60 s, but Ring-app Extended Live View runs up to 30 min, which means notice could come up to 30 min late. 'Within moments' is an overclaim.

7. Judges cannot exercise the deployed PWA without their own 30-minute Playground token. Ship a 'paste your Playground token' mode and a labelled replay mode, or the live URL will show an expired state through 20 Nov.

8. The central promise cannot be verified from India: catching live views opened in the owner's Ring app needs US hardware, a plan and account linking. It rests only on the doc line 'User or partner initiated a live view session'.

None of these is a hard blocker. Items 1-3 require dropping media from OnAir's own path.
RNG-3.demo_attack:
Beat 10-25 s, 'REAL' (Dana taps Check the front door; the aide's phone shows the notice instantly):
- The instant notice is OnAir's own app sending a message to its other app. It comes from the button tap, not from Ring data.
- The Ring contribution is just a WHEP stream, which is itself contested on the Playground.
- A sharp judge sees 'app A pushes to app B', which is a staged wow.

Beat 25-40 s, a console simulation shown as a live view from the Ring app or another app:
- This is the only beat that really comes from Ring data. The organizer confirms that the Package, Vehicle and Motion buttons write on_demand records, so the record is genuine.
- But in the console it is a 'Motion' button press, presented as a Ring-app live view, with a shifted demo clock. It is credible only if the stand-in is labelled on screen and a real wall-clock timer shows the actual poll-to-notice delay. A hard cut would hide that delay and make the beat look faked.

Beat 40-45 s: a fixture. Labelled and honest, but simulated.

Net: one of the three beats is real Ring-derived behaviour. The headline value (catching Ring-app live views) is only ever shown by a stand-in.

Story problems:
- The Playground device is an outdoor doorbell. A 'private hour 13:00-14:00' on a porch camera does not convince anyone, because worker privacy fears centre on indoor cameras and audio (Fi2W; Beverly).
- False reassurance: Beverly says families mostly use disclosed footage for after-the-fact checks such as 'confirming the 12:30 nap actually happened'. Reviewing recorded clips does not create on_demand records (inference: they are not live views). A worker who sees '0 live views today' may wrongly believe nobody watched. That is a design and ethics flaw a Ring privacy judge could raise.
- There is no AI or CV moment. Tech Implementation will be scored on how well the API is used, against Attest and nightlight, which look heavier.
RNG-3.differentiation_holds:
Partly. It is narrower than the concept claims.

Against native Ring:
- No native notice reaches the person being filmed. BGR: 'Ring does not officially state that any light means someone is actively watching'. The Indoor Cam light table lists 'recording', with no live-view-specific pattern.
- Event history is owner-side only.
- Native Modes can switch off Live View and Recording per camera for Disarmed, Home and Away (Ring support). The household can therefore already enforce a private hour natively. But Modes are not in the Partner API, OnAir cannot check them, and the worker gets no proof.
- Privacy Zones (up to two per device) exist natively. Only their count is readable, which supports the drift beat.

Against substitutes:
- Contract camera clauses with 'a dated acknowledgment' for each new camera, room or audio change are already standard practice (Beverly).
- The versioned agreement therefore copies a free norm. Only the runtime observation (session records checked against the agreement, plus drift) is new.

Against rivals:
- Attest shows brokered live views to the worker after the visit, but not as in-shift notice against an agreement.
- My limited search found no worker-facing product that alerts the person being filmed (low confidence: absence of evidence).
- Beside Care faces the care recipient.

The differentiation survives only if the pitch centres on 'Ring's own session records, checked against what both sides signed' and is framed as complementary to Attest ('Attest proves the visit happened; OnAir shows the camera was used as agreed'). As a 'compliance dashboard' it collapses into a contract clause.
RNG-3.redesign:
Make it 'OnAir: a metadata-only camera-use receipt', with the household announcing a check and Ring's record confirming it.

1. OnAir never touches media. Remove the brokered WHEP viewer and the production field-of-view frame.
   - The self-audit becomes true and checkable: OnAir only calls devices, status, configurations and history, so is_third_party_reviewed should stay false (verify on day 1).
   - It also works on TAKE devices, where video-reading partner apps get encrypted content (FAQ Q10). That is a Ring-specific, judge-legible advantage.
   - Camera coverage at signing comes from the device names plus household-written placement notes (room type, what is in view, audio on or off as a pledge). A Playground WHEP frame may appear only in the demo, clearly labelled, and opened by the stand-in tool below, not by OnAir.

2. Announce, then match, instead of attribution through OnAir's own viewer.
   - Before checking, the household taps 'I'm checking the front door: arrival check'. The worker gets that announcement at once; it is honestly real-time because it is a declaration.
   - When Ring's history later shows the on_demand record, OnAir matches it to the announcement. Classes:
     - announced and confirmed by Ring
     - announced, no record seen
     - unannounced (prompts a reason, logged in the ledger)
     - outside the agreed window or purpose
   - This turns the staged app-to-app beat into a check of the human's claim against Ring's own record.

3. The demo uses a separate, labelled 'Ring-app stand-in' tool: a browser WHEP session plus the Playground console buttons. It creates the on_demand records the poller finds, with a real wall-clock overlay. The promise becomes 'notice after the session, median N s measured over 20 trials', not 'within moments'.

4. Honest exposure in the receipt:
   - Add 'camera recorded N motion events during your shift' (production; fixture-labelled on the Playground).
   - Add a fixed line: 'OnAir cannot see playback of recorded clips or audio use.' This removes the false-reassurance problem.

5. Frame the camera honestly. The Playground doorbell is the 'arrival and door' camera. Indoor cameras are the production path. The agreement includes a private-quarters exclusion checklist (Virginia rule per Fi2W; Washington HB 2355 per a vendor blog, unverified against official text).

6. Position the product as complementary to Attest. Target placement agencies as the channel, since a household choosing it alone is the weak link.

7. Day-1 kill tests:
   - (a) A console button press and a browser WHEP session each yield an on_demand record within 5 min. If not, kill the concept.
   - (b) is_third_party_reviewed stays false when only metadata is called.
   - (c) Playground /configurations returns image_enhancements.privacy_zones and motion_detection.enabled.

8. Cut from the MVP: OnAir's own viewer and the field-of-view hashing. This saves about 8-10 h (estimate), to spend on latency instrumentation, the token-paste and replay modes for judges, and household-side access logs of OnAir's own calls (Content Policy §1.2.2).

Even with this redesign it remains a modest-scoring, low-risk entry. It fixes the contradictions, but not the buyer-incentive problem or the absence of a 'wow'.

strongest_rival_threat.rival: Spare AI Voice. Ecolane IVA and TripMaster IVA offer the same thing on other scheduling platforms.
strongest_rival_threat.why: Spare's product page says AI Voice answers rider calls, books trips, cancels rides and makes changes inside the agency's own scheduling system, so riders do not wait on hold. Listed use cases include after-hours booking, caregiver trip confirmation, paratransit ETA checks and multilingual voice plus SMS ('No new apps to download'). The product is shipping, not a concept. Metro Magazine (31 May 2024) names MVTA, Auburn, Milton and CapMetro as implementing it. PSTA's official press release (27 Aug 2025) says ADA paratransit (Access) riders can book, check status and cancel without waiting on hold, and that the system remembers favourite locations and payment methods (a $134k contract). Ecolane IVA (and TripMaster IVA) offers the same: 24/7, 30+ languages, and the example utterance 'Cancel my 3pm return trip', with a Via Mobility pilot. That is ALX-2's headline value ('book, change and cancel trips by voice instead of waiting on hold'), already delivered with real scheduler integration. It also runs on a phone every rider already owns, with no Echo, no Alexa+ subscription and no US-only add-on. The concept's rival table lists only apps, TripCheck and Uber, and misses this whole category.

ALX-2.eligibility_attack:
There is no hard rules blocker. Rules L298 and L343 accept a self-hosted MCP server (2025-11-25 or later) over Streamable HTTP, or a simulated Alexa+ experience 'built using any AI or agentic tool'. The repo must include the simulation source and the video must clearly show the simulation. Forum 45058 also allows deterministic runtime rules. Remaining eligibility risks:
(1) The OSS harness copies the schema of Amazon's gated certification-verdict.json, including the verdict values CERTIFIED/CONDITIONAL/NOT_CERTIFIED (Local Inspector doc). That can read as claiming an Amazon certification outcome. Use a different file name and schema with PASS/WARN/FAIL only, and add an 'unofficial' banner.
(2) The pitch says it implements Amazon's Functional Requirements 'literally', including 'linked return-trip protection'. The FR page (last updated 21 Jul 2026) has duplicate prevention, resumable purchase, read-back and policy/fee disclosure before cancel, but no linked-trip requirement. Presenting your own feature as an Amazon requirement invites a 'misleading claims' critique.
(3) Amazon's add-ons home lists ride booking as a partner-only Category SDK category. That does not make the entry ineligible, but it signals that Amazon treats ride booking as partner (Uber) territory.
(4) The hosted endpoint must stay live through 20 Nov (forum 45411), or the project must ship a local-run path.
(5) Real agency names may appear only as cited config sources, never as branding.
(6) The OSS mini needs a separately licensed repo or contribution; per forum 45310 that is fine.
ALX-2.feasibility_attack:
Feasible for a solo developer in 20 days. There is no blocker, but the 88 h estimate hides several sinks.
(a) Sessionful 2025-11-25 Streamable HTTP on Lambda + API Gateway (inference): SSE streams and server-to-client elicitation fit poorly there (API Gateway integration timeouts, no streaming on HTTP API). Plan for JSON-response mode with no elicitation and all state in DynamoDB, which also removes the 'MCP elicitation' line from the pitch.
(b) Cognito as the OAuth 2.1 server: you must serve RFC 9728 protected-resource metadata yourself, and Cognito has no Dynamic Client Registration, so the simulated host has to be pre-registered. That is roughly 6-10 h (estimate) for a flow judges never see. Swap it for a labelled, pre-linked test rider.
(c) The simulated host's language understanding is the trap. A deterministic grammar is allowed, but it makes 'arrive by 10 ... 10 is full ... I'll take 9:35' brittle and visibly scripted. An LLM host adds about 6-10 h (estimate) and Bedrock new-account quota risk (two forum reports of quota 0).
(d) Sending receipts through the SES sandbox requires verified recipients. That is fine for a test inbox.
(e) The 24 h harness is the first thing to cut if time runs short.
(f) An India-based developer with no paratransit contacts can only seed configs from public pages. The falsification test's 'one screen-reader user' is achievable remotely, but no real agency or rider validation is possible.
Net: buildable with about 20-30 h buffer if OAuth and the Echo Show carousel are trimmed (estimate).
ALX-2.demo_attack:
The 45 s wow is a scripted multi-turn booking against a mock scheduler whose '10 is full' is a seeded capacity value. Judges see hotel and restaurant booking flows constantly. The two non-trivial beats, the duplicate catch ('You already have trip LAT-4821') and the orphaned-return-leg prompt, last about 10 s and look like ordinary chatbot replies unless the video exposes the conditional write or trip graph. Even then they read as backend hygiene, not a new capability.

The voice-only 'Echo Dot' runs in a browser: a mic or text box plus TTS. That is credible, but it is not a wow. With a fictional agency and no riders, every impact statement is hypothetical.

A judge or AI-assisted reviewer who knows Spare or Ecolane will see an existing product category, already deployed at real agencies, rebuilt with a mock. Their public pages even host call recordings of trip booking.

Latent-LLM test:
- The conversational layer (intent parsing, slot filling, read-back phrasing, the 'cancel my morning ride' resolution) is exactly what Alexa+ and the vendors' LLM agents already do.
- The non-latent part (booking horizon, negotiation window, cancel cutoff, no-show points, idempotency) belongs, in any real deployment, to the agency's scheduler (Spare, Ecolane, Trapeze, Via).
- A real add-on would therefore shrink to an MCP layer over that scheduler's API. That is the rules' L443 'Obvious: basic MCP wrapper around an existing API', with the mock policy engine as duplicated logic.
ALX-2.differentiation_holds:
No.
(1) Voice booking, changes and cancellations without hold time: already shipped by Spare AI Voice (2024-, PSTA 2025), Ecolane IVA and TripMaster IVA, all integrated with real schedulers and available 24/7. DREDF also notes that some agencies already take bookings through IVR.
(2) Self-service booking: already offered by myRTCpara (book, check, cancel, track), the Via-powered Alexandria DOT app (one-time and round trips, edit or cancel until 4:30pm the day before), MATBUS, STA PassApp and RTS Plus.
(3) Voice ride booking on Alexa+: native through Uber, and ride booking is a partner-gated Category SDK category.
(4) Read-back, explicit yes, fare breakdown, receipts, duplicate prevention, stable IDs, max 5 options: these are certification table stakes every transactional add-on must meet (FR §8, §9, §13), not originality.

The residual delta is narrow:
- The Echo channel for paratransit. No existing Alexa paratransit-booking skill surfaced in two searches, which is a weak negative.
- A linked-leg orphan prompt and late-cancel policy disclosure. These are small UX features; whether the vendor agents already do them is unverified. Ecolane's own example handles 'cancel my 3pm return trip'.
- An OSS harness adjacent to mcp-voice-simulator and everyword.

Crowding is genuinely low: a GitHub search for paratransit repos created after 31 Aug returned 2 repos, neither of them Alexa+. But being uncrowded is not the same as being differentiated.
ALX-2.redesign:
Not recommended as the primary-track thesis. No narrower paratransit framing restores originality.
- Caregiver confirmation is already in Spare.
- Arrival call-outs and texts already exist: Access LA call-outs and Pace TripCheck imminent-arrival alerts.
- Rider-side no-show protection needs agency data the add-on cannot have.
- 'Alexa+ channel adapter for an agency's existing scheduler' is the rules' Obvious wrapper.

Salvage one component: the conformance harness as the Open Source mini contribution, attached to whichever primary project is chosen. Specify it as follows:
- A separate MIT repo, e.g. 'addon-fr-checks'.
- A CLI that connects to any MCP server over Streamable HTTP, negotiating 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18 and 2025-11-25.
- It replays scripted lifecycles: create, modify one parameter, status, duplicate attempt, cancel without confirmation, interrupted purchase then resume, and invalid parameters.
- It asserts about 12 machine-checkable rules from FR §8 and §13: every tools/list entry is invocable; inputSchema is valid and enforced; isError is used rather than malformed payloads; IDs chain from search to details to book; duplicate requests return the existing ID; destructive tools refuse without a confirmation token; the charged amount equals the quoted amount; no tool names, JSON or internal IDs appear in customer-facing text.
- It emits its own JSON schema with PASS/WARN/FAIL values, not the gated certification-verdict.json shape or 'CERTIFIED' strings, with the banner 'unofficial; not Amazon certification'.
- It includes tests and a tiny reference server.
The §9 voice-only rules (max 5 options, read-back) can be checked only heuristically against the text content, so label those checks WARN-only.

strongest_rival_threat.rival: Apple Magnifier for Mac with Accessibility Reader (Reader Mode), using an iPhone on a stand via Continuity Camera / Desk View
strongest_rival_threat.why: Apple announced this on 13 May 2025 and its accessibility features page now describes it in the present tense. It already does BigPrint's core loop for low-vision users, for free and first-party. An iPhone on a stand is the camera (Continuity Camera; documents via Desk View). The large screen is the display. The user captures a frame and Reader Mode turns the text into a custom legible format: font, size, colour and spacing. The text can be read aloud (Speak Screen), and there are audible prompts for framing the document. So the 'phone on a stand + big-screen reflow + read aloud' half of BigPrint is no longer novel. Free phone apps cover the rest: Seeing AI (Document channel with alignment audio cues, plus 'Ask Seeing AI about the contents') and Google Lookout (Documents mode, Q&A on images). Fire TV's own Miracast display mirroring can also put any Android phone magnifier on the TV for $0. That native mirroring is verified on the Amazon help page; whether Vega devices support it is not verified. What remains for BigPrint, and is not verified in any rival: (1) the TV plus remote as the only control surface, with a fixed phone the user never touches; (2) every fact shown with a zoomed crop of where it is printed, plus a confidence gate ('Not sure, show me'); (3) Android/Fire TV households, which cannot use Apple's Mac+iPhone route (inference).

FTV-3.eligibility_attack:
No hard blocker under the Official Rules.
(1) Fire TV rule (Rules L296/L341): the project must run on Fire OS or Vega OS, and the video must show it on a real Fire TV or the Fire TV/Vega simulator. A Vega app on the VVD satisfies this. The phone is an auxiliary sensor and nothing prohibits it. However, the video must show the Vega app doing the work, not just the phone.
(2) Video trademark clause (Rules: 'must not include third party trademarks ... unless the Entrant has permission'): a real electricity bill carries a utility's name and logo, and a comparison slide showing Apple, Seeing AI or Lookout UI or logos is also risky. Use only synthetic, labelled bills with invented sender names. Keep competitor comparisons in the text description, without logos.
(3) Testing clause: the project must be free and unrestricted for judges until judging ends. Keep the AWS backend live through 20 Nov. Add a judge path that needs no stand, such as 'upload a sample image' on the phone page plus bundled sample documents, because judges are unlikely to have the stand setup.
(4) The proprietary-hardware clause (L391) is not triggered, since a phone and a Fire TV are widely available.
(5) India is not an excluded country (rules L238 list).
(6) The organizer's 'latent LLM capability scores poorly' remark (forum 45397) was about Alexa+. The same logic would plausibly hit Quality of the Idea here, because 'what is this bill, how much, when due' is single-turn vision Q&A. Seeing AI, Lookout, and Alexa+ ('document and photo understanding', per a third-party review) already do it. This is a scoring risk, not an eligibility failure.
FTV-3.feasibility_attack:
(1) The time budget is not credible as written. 115 h of work against about 117 h of capacity leaves about 2 h of buffer for a solo developer building 6 surfaces: the Vega app, the phone kiosk, the helper page, a backend of 8+ AWS services (API GW WebSocket, Lambda, S3+KMS, Textract, Bedrock, Polly, DynamoDB), a 30-document evaluation and an OSS package, plus video, friction log and feedback. Known setup tax adds to this. macOS 27 removed Rosetta. Node is v25 but the samples pin Node 18–20. The VVD crashes when free memory falls below 2 GB on a 24 GB Mac that will also be screen-recording (firetv.md §2–3).
(2) Capture resolution is a hard technical constraint the concept missed. The Textract limits page says the minimum detectable text height is 15 px, which is 8 pt at 150 DPI. A 1080p frame grabbed from getUserMedia gives roughly 92–130 DPI on an A4 page (computed inference), so small print on bills will drop out. A true full-resolution still needs ImageCapture.takePhoto(). caniuse shows it supported on Chrome for Android but not on Safari iOS (through 27.2). The kiosk must therefore be Android Chrome, or request a 4K stream, which is unverified per device.
(3) Character set: the Textract FAQ says it detects the 'Standard English alphabet and ASCII symbols'. The pitch's '₹2,340' likely will not come back as ₹ (inference). If Nova adds the symbol back, the 'verbatim, checkable' claim breaks.
(4) Language: Queries are English-only (verified in the limits doc). That is fine for the MVP, but it weakens the India story.
(5) Vega WebSocket: the RN-for-Vega 0.83 network page now shows a WebSocket section (FC-scrape this session). It is mirrored upstream React Native documentation, and runtime behaviour on the VVD is untested. VoiceView on the VVD rests on one entrant's anecdote.
(6) The Fire OS fallback is not cheap. It means a second react-native-tvos build. AQC Live Device Interaction does not offer the Vega 4K Select (community thread, May 2026). A real Vega take therefore needs a purchased ₹5,499 stick and `vega devmode` (one forum success, one Reddit failure; anecdotal).
(7) Bedrock quota-0 reports on new accounts (2 forum reports) are a day-1 risk. Removing Nova from the critical path eliminates it.
FTV-3.demo_attack:
(1) The wow timestamp is probably staged. The storyboard shows the card at 0:04 after OK. The real chain from India is: WSS to us-east-1, then the phone shutter, a 3–8 MB JPEG upload over home Wi-Fi, the S3 event, Lambda, synchronous AnalyzeDocument QUERIES+LAYOUT, Nova Lite, Polly, DynamoDB, and the push to the VVD. That plausibly takes about 6–12 s; this is an estimate and has not been measured. A cut at that moment is exactly what a skeptical judge looks for.
(2) The 'TV' in the demo is a Mac window. On a laptop screen the VVD loses the 10-foot, large-display premise that the whole removal test rests on.
(3) Two devices and a document have to be visible together. That needs a second camera and a composite, and those edits again invite 'is this real?'.
(4) The ₹ glyph on the hero card may not survive Textract (FAQ: ASCII symbols).
(5) The users are simulated (teammates wearing low-vision glasses). That is acceptable if labelled, but it weakens Impact.
(6) The 'Send to Priya' ending is the least differentiated beat, since sharing a card is commodity.
What would make the wow real: one unedited take with a visible on-screen elapsed timer, covering OK press → reflowed text → fact card → 'Show me' zoom. Show the honest latency, with a progress state. Then show a deliberately smudged or folded field producing 'Not sure, show me' instead of a guess. Display the VVD full-screen on an actual TV over HDMI, captioned 'Vega Virtual Device', or use a real 4K Select. Picture-in-picture a fixed camera on the phone and the document. Use a synthetic USD (or 'Rs.') bill labelled 'synthetic sample'.
FTV-3.differentiation_holds:
Narrowly, and only if the thesis moves. The magnifier half (phone on a stand + big-screen reflow + read aloud) collapses against Apple Magnifier for Mac with Accessibility Reader Mode, which is free and first-party and offers capture-frame, custom font/colour/size, framing prompts and Speak Screen. It also collapses against free phone readers (Seeing AI Document channel, Lookout Documents mode) and Fire TV's native Miracast mirroring of any Android magnifier.
The fact-card half ('who sent it, how much, by when') is a latent multimodal-LLM capability. Seeing AI ('Ask about the contents'), Lookout (image Q&A) and, per a third-party review, Alexa+ (document/photo understanding, also on Fire TV) already answer it. Visible entrants do not collide: GitHub searches for fire tv + textract/ocr/magnifier/document reader found 0 repos created after 15 Aug 2026. vikrant-29/ai-tv-vision-assistant describes photos from a bundled offline dataset, reads no documents, and its backend has never been deployed. The rest of the accessibility cluster is audio description plus one large-target TV UI (simple-mode).
What survives, with no rival verified to do it:
- Remote-only capture on the TV, with a fixed phone the user never touches (Apple's route needs a Mac and an iPhone, and the phone apps need hand aiming and touch).
- Every fact is a non-generative extraction (Textract QUERY_RESULT) shown beside a geometry-cropped zoom of the source, with a confidence gate. This directly addresses a reported Alexa+ weakness: a third-party reviewer found its document extraction 'selective' and missing dates (anecdotal).
That is a defensible wedge, but much narrower than the pitch claims. Originality should be scored on the verification loop and the 10-foot remote-only interaction, not on reflow or reading aloud.
FTV-3.redesign:
Rename and rescope to 'BigPrint Mail Check': one job, checking a single letter or bill on the TV with the remote alone, where every fact can be verified by eye.
(1) Thesis: lead with 'Show me' evidence zoom plus the 'Not sure' gate plus no-touch remote capture. Do not claim reflow or read-aloud as novel; Apple ships them.
(2) Take Bedrock off the critical path. The card is built only from Textract AnalyzeDocument QUERY_RESULT text, Confidence and Geometry, using at most 6 English queries: sender, document type, amount due, due date, requested action, reference number (masked to the last 4 digits). A deterministic sentence template turns these into plain language. Any field below a 90% confidence threshold renders as 'Not sure, show me'; Textract best practices say financial workflows may need thresholds of 90% or higher. This removes hallucination risk, the Bedrock quota-0 risk, and the 'latent LLM' critique. Nova can return later as an optional, clearly labelled 'explain in plain words' button that cites line IDs.
(3) The reflow view uses LAYOUT/LINE blocks with D-pad line-stepping, bound to KeplerA11ySettingsInterfaceTurbo caption styles, plus Polly sentence speech marks.
(4) Phone kiosk: Android Chrome only, using ImageCapture.takePhoto() for full-resolution stills (unsupported on Safari iOS per caniuse). Add a printed placement mat with corner marks and a desk lamp. If fewer than a minimum number of LINE blocks come back, the TV says 'Move the letter into the box', so it never shows a guessed card.
(5) Cut the helper share to a stretch goal. If time allows, add a read-only card link, sent only after an on-TV confirmation.
(6) Command channel: WSS on Vega, with a pre-built HTTPS long-poll fallback.
(7) OSS mini challenge: publish only the focus-safe zoom-to-normalized-bounding-box viewer and the D-pad line stepper for RN for Vega, with jest tests for the geometry and focus order.
(8) Day-2 kill gates. (a) On 10 synthetic or own redacted English documents captured on the stand under lamp light, at least 9 of 10 QUERY fields are correct and no more than 20% fall below the threshold. If this fails, kill, because without verifiable facts this is a weaker Apple Reader Mode on a TV. (b) Measure p50 latency from OK to card, India to us-east-1. If it is over about 10 s, show staged progress (reflow first, card second) and state the real number in the video. (c) The VVD opens a wss connection to API Gateway; if not, switch to long-poll.
(9) Video: as in the demo fix, one unedited timed take on a TV showing the VVD (or a real 4K Select), synthetic labelled documents, a visible 'Not sure' state, no third-party logos, and competitor comparisons kept in the text only.
Re-estimated effort: about 95–100 h solo, leaving about 15–20 h of buffer. This is an estimate.

evidence_checked.finding: Apple press release, 13 May 2025: Magnifier for Mac works with Continuity Camera on iPhone and USB cameras, 'supports reading documents using Desk View', and is integrated with Accessibility Reader, which 'transforms text from the physical world into a custom legible format' (font, colour, spacing, Spoken Content). Saved in .firecrawl/idea-redteam-ftv3-apple-magnifier-mac.json.

Apple features page describes Reader Mode in the present tense: capture a frame of text; adjust font, size and colour; get audible guidance on framing and perspective; read aloud with Speak Screen or Speak Selection. Magnifier for Mac is listed as an 'Update'.

Seeing AI is free. Its Document channel uses alignment audio cues to capture a printed page, and users can 'Ask Seeing AI about the contents'. One user review mentions using it to spot-check mail. Saved in .firecrawl/idea-redteam-ftv3-phone-doc-readers.json.
Google Lookout is free. Documents mode captures a whole page in 30+ languages, Text mode is pitched for 'sorting mail', and Images mode offers Q&A (English only).

Echo Show vision accessibility includes Show and Tell (identify held items) and Alexa+ Visual Input (identify objects, assist with daily tasks). Reading letters or bills is not stated. Saved in .firecrawl/idea-gate-echo-vision-a11y.md.

Third-party review (anecdotal): Alexa+ adds 'document and photo understanding' and reaches Fire TV. Document extraction was 'selective', missing dates. This supports the grounding wedge but also shows an Amazon-native Q&A path exists.

Fire TV natively supports display mirroring from Miracast Android devices (Settings > Display & Sounds > Enable Display Mirroring); iOS and macOS are not supported. Support on Vega devices is not verified. This means a $0 phone-magnifier-on-TV substitute exists.
Query detection is English-only. Minimum detectable text height is 15 px (8 pt at 150 DPI). Up to 15 queries per page synchronously. Images must be 10,000 px or less per side.
Textract detects printed text and handwriting from the 'Standard English alphabet and ASCII symbols', so the ₹ in the demo storyboard is at risk. Queries are English only.
Recommends images of at least 150 DPI, and says workflows involving financial decisions might need confidence thresholds of 90% or higher. Supports the confidence-gate design.
ImageCapture (takePhoto) is not supported on Safari iOS through 27.2 and is supported on Chrome for Android. Full-resolution kiosk stills therefore need Android Chrome.

The RN-for-Vega 0.83 network page includes a WebSocket section (FC-scrape, .firecrawl/idea-judge-vega-network.md). It is mirrored upstream React Native documentation, and runtime behaviour on the VVD is not verified.

The README says it describes images from a bundled offline demo dataset. Its Bedrock backend has 'never been deployed or executed'. It runs on Fire OS via Flutter and does no physical-document capture, so collision is low.

Searches for repos created after 15 Aug 2026: 'fire tv textract', 'fire tv ocr', 'fire tv magnifier' and 'fire tv document reader' returned 0. 'fire tv accessibility' returned 10, mostly audio description, plus rogerkorantenng/simple-mode (large-target TV UI) and Mantel (dementia). None reads documents. The unauthenticated rate limit was hit after 14 queries, so coverage is incomplete.
Forum snippet: the Fire TV Stick Select (Vega) is not available in AQC Live Device Interaction. A real-device Vega take therefore needs a purchased stick.

Fire TV: the project must run on Fire OS or Vega OS, and the video must show it on a device or the Fire TV/Vega simulator (L341). The video must not include third-party trademarks without permission. Judges must have free testing access until judging ends. India is not excluded.

strongest_rival_threat.rival: ProofClock, together with School Bus Home (both from the same developer, erbacciltd, on the Ring Appstore)
strongest_rival_threat.why: ProofClock already ships CurbClock's 'original mechanism' in general form. From Ring motion timestamps alone, it records when someone arrived, how long they stayed and whether they met the window. It issues a verdict (Verified, Short, No-show or Unverifiable) and exports a monthly CSV 'for billing and SLA disputes'. Its sibling School Bus Home (https://ring.com/appstore/school-bus-home) adds the rest: an expected window at entry cameras, vehicle-class detection (a US yellow school bus), a confirming still kept 31 days, and a 'no bus by expected time' heads-up. Combined, the two cover about 70% of CurbClock: window, vehicle at the entrance, dwell, verdict, dispute export and a kept frame. That share is my estimate. TAKE makes the overlap worse. TAKE is becoming the default encryption for all Ring customers, and during rollout partner apps cannot read clips or snapshots or open live streams on TAKE devices (developer FAQ Q10). On real devices CurbClock's CV path therefore degrades to metadata-only dwell, which is exactly ProofClock's design. What no reviewed rival offers: paratransit rule clauses (early-arrival anchor, 5-minute wait, dispute deadline), a live countdown for the rider, helper acceptance with escalation, and an agency-specific dispute letter.

RNG-1.eligibility_attack: Passes, with fixes needed. (1) Runtime hook (rules section 4, M16/M17): the Playground token, the device/status/capabilities reads, WHEP live view and event history are documented Ring surfaces that are actually called. The FAQ names the Playground as an acceptable simulator. Forum 45309 (DevRel) calls it 'the only documented route that needs neither a US device nor an account link'. (2) ring-sandbox is a third-party emulator built by another entrant and is not listed in Ring's docs, so it cannot count as the Ring technology. It is acceptable only as a labelled test harness. If the Playground calls fail, the Ring requirement rests on device reads alone, which is Stage-1-thin. (3) Playground footage is third-party CC BY material. The rules bar third-party copyrighted material without permission, and the FAQ says brief attributed footage is 'typically fine' but to check with organizers. Attribute it on screen and in the README, and ask in the forum under Rule 11.6. (4) Two anecdotes in the concept, a 'WHEP failure 2026-09-30' and a '68 KB JPEG' snapshot, could not be found in research_sweep_results.json or anywhere in .firecrawl/. They must not appear in the submission; repeating them would be unsourced. (5) Team-recorded street footage must blur bystanders and drop plates. That is a privacy hygiene issue, not a rules blocker. (6) No ineligibility for India-resident entrants (rules section 3). No hard eligibility blocker found.
RNG-1.feasibility_attack:
The solo 105 h estimate (estimate) is about 5.8 h/day over 18 working days once 2 recovery days are reserved. The MVP spans roughly 11 subsystems across browser CV, Python Lambdas, two PWAs with Web Push, PDF generation, an emulator harness and six AWS services, plus Firecrawl onboarding. That is too wide for one person; trimmed, it is roughly 80 h (estimate).

Day-1 unknowns:
(a) Whether the Playground opens for an India-based Amazon Developer account. This is unverified, and the console sits behind sign-in.
(b) What the Vehicle simulation shows. No entrant has published a Vehicle frame. The one Playground frame on record (doorstep-ring) is the package clip 'Thief stealing our package'. That entrant's vehicle scenario used an AI-generated driveway image, which suggests a usable Vehicle frame was not captured (inference).
(c) WHEP. This risk is lower than the concept states. DevRel in forum 45309 says a 500 is 'likely' caused by sending the offer before ICE gathering completes, and doorstep-ring got a 201 and 1280x720 frames with a headless-Chrome offer on 2026-09-23.

Structural problems for the real-device path:
- TAKE is the default for all customers worldwide once rolled out. Partner live view, clips and snapshots then return encrypted content, so the CV witness and evidence frames fail for most future households.
- The UX guide forbids analysing video inside privacy zones, and many owners mask the street.
- Motion events fire only inside motion zones, and Smart Alerts can silently suppress events.
- Parked cars and delivery vans in the curb polygon cause false 'vehicle at your curb' triggers. With fleet-number OCR deliberately excluded, the detector cannot tell the paratransit van from any other vehicle.
- Node v25 vs Next 14: use nvm.

Bedrock and Firecrawl are unnecessary for the core and should be cut.
RNG-1.demo_attack:
The only REAL Ring segment of the wow moment is live view of pre-recorded Playground footage with a bounding box drawn on a car. That is close to the rules' own 'Obvious' Ring example (motion alert, basic live view). Everything that makes the idea matter is SIMULATED: vehicle arrival as a webhook, the early departure at 2:09:10, the 'candidate agency-error' and the dispute packet. Those parts are a third-party emulator replaying team-recorded footage shot on an Indian street, scripted to depart early. A judge will read the decisive moment as staged, and the vehicle on screen will not look like a US paratransit cutaway.

Ring's own native features also undercut the 'vehicle at your curb' beat:
- Smart Alerts send vehicle alerts.
- Video Descriptions plus Echo Show 8/11 support 'Alexa, tell me when the pizza is delivered' (Ring support article).
- Shared Users receive the same motion notifications as the owner (Ring Community snippet).
- At least one agency already pushes an arrival notification: Valley Metro says 'You will receive a notification when your vehicle has arrived' alongside its 5-minute wait (search snippet).

The countdown and helper-accept UI is believable but generic.

The packet framing is fragile. Blurring people also hides the rider's own readiness, and 'no vehicle seen' is not proof that no vehicle came, because of camera field of view, night conditions and recall. Two searches found no agency source that accepts rider video in no-show disputes; RideRTA's stated remedy is to phone the dispatcher.
RNG-1.differentiation_holds:
Partially. It is not a latent-LLM idea: the core is a deterministic policy evaluator, timers and CV, and the LLM pieces (Nova letter rephrasing, Firecrawl JSON extraction) are optional and should be cut. It does not collapse completely either. Among the 56 Ring Appstore listings, the roughly 36 visible hackathon Ring repos and the agency apps reviewed, none combines paratransit no-show rule clauses, a policy-anchored wait clock shown to the rider, named-helper acceptance with escalation, and an agency-specific dispute letter with a deadline. The domain is also uncrowded in the hackathon field.

Each component taken alone is not new:
- Vehicle-arrival alerting is native (Ring Smart Alerts, Video Descriptions with Alexa, Shared Users) and agency-provided (Valley Metro arrival notification, Pace TripCheck imminent-arrival alert, dispatcher calls per DREDF).
- The window-plus-vehicle-plus-kept-evidence pattern is School Bus Home.
- The arrival-plus-dwell-plus-window-plus-verdict-plus-dispute-export evaluator is ProofClock.

The concept's originality claim of 4 is overstated. What is defensible is the paratransit-specific workflow layer, not the 'policy-as-code dwell evaluation' mechanism. The 'Ring as independent witness' thesis is weakened by TAKE, by the inability to identify the vehicle, and by agency acceptance being unverified.
RNG-1.redesign:
Narrow it to 'CurbClock: a human-confirmed, policy-anchored pickup log'. Drop CV-as-witness as the thesis.

(1) Trigger and identification. A vehicle event opens a 60 s Ring live view on the helper's phone through a server-proxied WHEP exchange with a browser-built offer. The vehicle event is a motion_detected sub_type=vehicle webhook: labelled SIMULATED in the demo, real only on US devices. The rider can also tap 'my ride should be here' to open the same view. Live view is REAL on the Playground. The in-browser detector box is only a hint. The helper, or a sighted rider, answers 'Is this your ride? Yes / No / Can't tell', and only 'Yes' starts the clock. This replaces unverifiable CV identification with a human confirmation backed by a watermarked Ring frame and the on_demand history entry Ring logs for that session (REAL, readable on the Playground per doorstep-ring and forum 45309). It also makes the Playground calls load-bearing even if the Vehicle footage turns out to be generic.

(2) Clock. Fully model ONE agency policy (Union City or Access Services LA), including the early-arrival rule that starts the 5 minutes at the scheduled time. Include two more agency policies as schema data only. EventBridge Scheduler holds the clock and the helper ladder (primary, then backup, 60 s timeout). The rider PWA speaks the countdown and shows it in large type (WCAG 2.2 AA).

(3) Departure. A second live check, or the vehicle-event end (SIMULATED), confirmed by the helper.

(4) Output. Reframe the dispute packet as an 'AVL review request'. It is a one-page letter that quotes the agency's own clause, gives the rider-side timeline (helper-confirmed arrival and departure, Ring live-view session IDs and history timestamps) and at most 2 watermarked frames. It asks the agency to check its own AVL/MDT records for that trip before the dispute deadline. It never claims proof, and never claims the agency accepts rider video.

(5) Cut Firecrawl onboarding, Bedrock, SQS, multi-agency extraction and the offline clip recompute. Keep API Gateway + Lambda (HMAC over raw bytes, 2xx under 5 s, dedupe on meta.request_id), DynamoDB, Scheduler, S3 lifecycle and the open-source policy schema/evaluator with table tests. Target 80 h or less (estimate).

(6) State the following in the README and video:
- On TAKE devices, partner live view, clips and snapshots are encrypted during rollout, so the real-device path falls back to vehicle-event metadata plus helper confirmation in the native Ring app.
- Ring says support for the most recent 24 h of TAKE video is being worked on.
- Agency acceptance of rider-side records is unverified.

(7) Day-1 kill switches. Drop the concept if any of these holds:
- the Playground does not open for an India account;
- WHEP succeeds on fewer than 3 of 10 attempts with a browser offer sent after ICE gathering completes;
- a read of 10 more agency policies shows no written dispute or appeal path for a 'driver did not wait' claim.

(8) Demo, 45 s, in this order:
1. REAL: Playground live view on the helper's phone.
2. The helper taps 'Yes, that's my ride'.
3. The rider's tablet speaks 'Your ride is here; the driver waits until 2:12'.
4. The helper taps Accept.
5. SIMULATED (labelled) departure at 2 min 10 s.
6. The AVL review request is generated, quoting the clause and the deadline.

Remove the untraceable 'WHEP failure 2026-09-30' and '68 KB JPEG' claims.
